sentences.text: Angistorhinus is an extinct genus of phytosaur known for its narrow or hook-shaped snout.
It resembled Parasuchus but had nostrils positioned further back, closer to and above the eyes.
This massive animal had a skull length of 120–124 cm and an estimated total length of 7 to 8 meters.
Its teeth possessed the thickest enamel in absolute terms among phytosaurs, yet the lowest enamel thickness relative to crown size.
The genus was first named by Mehl in 1913, with Angistorhinus grandis designated as the type species.
In 2010, Michelle R. Stocker retained the validity of both Brachysuchus and A. grandis.
Angistorhinus belongs to the subfamily Mystriosuchinae and is classified within the family Parasuchidae.
Angistorhinus lived during the Carnian to Norian stages of the Triassic, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
Researchers Hungerbühler and Sues hypothesized in 2001 that Angistorhinus is a junior synonym of Rutiodon.
